Refit a model from several random seeds and check whether it reaches the same solution

Source: R/sensitivity.R
sensitivity.Rd

sensitivity() refits a fitted mixture model from several random seeds and reports whether the refits reach the same solution. Mixture-model estimation can converge to different local maxima, yielding different class assignments for the same data and model specification, so a solution that only one seed finds should not be interpreted.

Each seed gives one refit of the same model to the same data. The function records the refit's log likelihood, whether it converged and how many iterations it took, and compares its class assignments with those of the reference fit, after aligning the class labels. Log likelihoods within tolerance of each other are grouped as one optimum, so the table shows how many seeds reached the best one and whether those that did assign the same observations to the same classes.

Usage

sensitivity(
  x,
  data = NULL,
  seeds = 1:10,
  n_starts = NULL,
  max_iter = NULL,
  tol = NULL,
  tolerance = NULL,
  cores = 1L
)

Arguments

x

The reference fit. Accepted:

  • a profile or class fit from lpa(), lca(), multilpa() or multilca() without membership covariates. A fit_staged() result varies the second-stage starts while holding its first-stage measurement solution fixed;

  • a transition fit from lta(), which also needs data;

  • a growth mixture (mixture_regression() with random).

Refused with latents_unsupported_sensitivity: a membership-covariate fit, and a directly fitted model with measurement blocks held fixed (fixed), because its original free starting values are not retained. Refused with latents_not_a_fit: the other multilpa() families (additive, dispersion and cross-level) and a mixture regression without random.

data

The data the model was fitted to, in its original row order. Optional for a profile or class fit and for a growth mixture, which carry the columns they were built from; required for an lta() fit (latents_bad_argument otherwise). Shared identifier and indicator columns are checked against the fit (latents_bad_inference_data).

seeds

At least two distinct integer seeds accepted by set.seed(). Default 1:10. Invalid values raise latents_bad_argument. Reusing the reference seed reproduces its initialisation when the other fitting controls are unchanged.

n_starts

Starts per refit. Defaults to the number the reference fit used.

max_iter, tol

Passed to each refit. Default to the reference fit's (for a fit that does not record them, to the defaults of the function that fitted it).

tolerance

Maximum log-likelihood difference for grouping refits. Each group is anchored at its highest log likelihood and spans no more than tolerance. Only converged refits receive an optimum index or a best flag. Defaults to the reference fit's replication tolerance, 1e-6 per observed value.

cores

Number of processor cores (default 1). The seeds are refitted in parallel, one seed per worker at a time, each refit on one core. Every refit sets its own seed, so the result is identical to cores = 1. Workers are forked processes on macOS and Linux, and a socket cluster on Windows and on macOS with Apple's Accelerate BLAS, as in multilpa(); socket workers load the installed copy of the package. More cores than seeds are not used.

Value

A data.frame of class latents_sensitivity (which plot() draws), one row per seed, in the order of seeds, with the columns

seed

integer: the seed of the refit.

log_likelihood

numeric: the refit's maximised log likelihood.

converged

logical: whether the refit met its convergence criterion.

iterations

integer: the number of iterations the refit reports.

optimum

integer: 1 for the group of converged refits holding the highest log likelihood, 2 for the next lower group, and so on; NA for a refit that did not converge.

best

logical: whether the refit converged to optimum 1.

agreement

numeric, 0 to 1: the proportion of units given the same class as in the reference fit, after label matching. The units are the observations of a profile or class fit, the occasions of a transition fit (profiles matched on the measurement) and the persons of a growth mixture (classes matched by their posterior memberships of the fitted persons). For profile and transition models, only observations included in both fits under their drop_empty settings are compared.

A failed refit has NA in every column except seed, and the call warns with latents_sensitivity_dropped. The reference fit itself is not a row of the table. Invalid arguments raise latents_bad_argument; see x and data for the other refusals.

as.data.frame() returns a plain data.frame. plot() accepts main and subtitle and returns a ggplot object showing each refit's log-likelihood difference from the best converged refit and its classification agreement with the reference fit. Unfinished refits are distinguished from converged maxima; if none converged, the highest observed log likelihood is the reference instead.

Details

Replication across seeds complements replication across starts within one fit. Each refit uses the reference fit's estimation controls unless alternatives are supplied.

A seed whose refit fails gives a row with NA estimates, and a latents_sensitivity_dropped warning reports how many seeds failed.

Interpretation

Consistent results across converged refits support numerical reproducibility, but do not guarantee a global maximum or establish the validity of the model. Similar likelihood values alone do not imply identical parameter estimates. The analysis assesses sensitivity to initialisation, rather than uncertainty arising from sampling or model selection.

See also

enumerate_classes() to vary the number of classes, and parameter_inference() for uncertainty about the parameters of a single solution.

Examples

set.seed(7)
example_data <- data.frame(
  school = rep(seq_len(12), each = 10),
  score_a = c(rnorm(60, -1.5), rnorm(60, 1.5)),
  score_b = c(rnorm(60, -1), rnorm(60, 1))
)
fit <- multilpa(example_data, c("score_a", "score_b"), "school",
                n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 1, n_starts = 3, seed = 1)
sensitivity(fit, seeds = 1:3, n_starts = 3)
#>   seed log_likelihood converged iterations optimum best agreement
#> 1    1      -396.1633      TRUE          9       1 TRUE         1
#> 2    2      -396.1633      TRUE          9       1 TRUE         1
#> 3    3      -396.1633      TRUE          9       1 TRUE         1

# Growth mixtures are known for local solutions.
growth <- mixture_regression(score ~ wave, data = subset(growth_scores, student <= 60),
                             n_classes = 2, id = "student", class_level = "group",
                             random = ~ 1, n_starts = 1, seed = 1)
sensitivity(growth, seeds = 1:2)
#>   seed log_likelihood converged iterations optimum best agreement
#> 1    1      -1175.788      TRUE         81       1 TRUE         1
#> 2    2      -1175.788      TRUE         81       1 TRUE         1
